Prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket are facing intense regulatory scrutiny and legal challenges as they rapidly integrate into mainstream financial news and influence upcoming midterm election discourse.

### Key Points
- Platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket are currently operating in a regulatory gray zone, with over 50 lawsuits pending regarding their classification as financial exchanges versus illegal gambling.
- Donald Trump Jr.’s venture firm, 1789 Capital, is a lead investor in Polymarket, and he serves as a paid adviser to both Polymarket and Kalshi.
- These companies are aggressively lobbying lawmakers and hiring former Biden administration officials to maintain their status as federally regulated financial exchanges.
- Mainstream media outlets, including CNN, CNBC, and Dow Jones, have integrated prediction market data into their coverage, granting the platforms significant public legitimacy.
- Election officials have expressed concerns that misleading social media posts and potential market manipulation by these platforms could incite voter discord during the midterm elections.

### Why it Matters
The rapid rise of prediction markets threatens to commodify democratic processes and blur the lines between speculative gambling and objective political analysis. As these platforms gain mainstream credibility, their influence on public sentiment and election integrity poses significant, poorly understood risks to the democratic landscape.

articles.title: The Brand-New Apple Watch Ultra 4 Is Already $99 Off, A New Low for This Model
articles.author: Oliver Haslam
articles.content:
Save $99: The Apple Watch Ultra 4 has only been on sale for a few weeks, but you can already get one with a massive $99 off — slashing the price to a new low price of just $700.
That’s the price you’ll pay for the black titanium model with a burgundy trail loop, but be sure to check your preferred color and band combo, as prices can fluctuate at a moment’s notice.
The Apple Watch Ultra 4 comes in a large 49mm size, which is easier to read when you’re on the go. The larger size also means the Apple Watch Ultra 4 can have an even bigger battery, providing over two days of battery life from a single charge. That’s vital if you’re camping or just want to get through more than a day of activity tracking and sleep monitoring.
More from CNET
This latest model brings Apple’s Siri AI to the wrist, and there are upgraded heart rate sensors to allow the Apple Watch Ultra 4 to capture measurements more regularly. And because this is an Apple Watch Ultra, it comes with cellular connectivity built right in so you can use your watch without taking your iPhone with you.
Alternatives you might like
If you’d prefer to spend even less, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 offers many of the same features as the Ultra 4 and is on sale for just $649. Options include the black titanium with black Alpine loop and black titanium with black ocean band. But again, these prices can fluctuate, so be sure to check all of the options before ordering.

articles.title: FBI arrests suspected member of ShinyHunters in connection with jobs site hack
articles.author: Sarah N. Lynch, Nicole  Sganga, Pat  Milton
articles.content:
Washington — The FBI this week arrested another individual suspected of being connected to ShinyHunters, the cybercriminal group that and stole personal data about its employees, FBI Director Kash Patel said on Friday.
"This is the latest arrest this FBI has made in a matter of days involving this network, as we work non-stop to dismantle the group, pursue new leads and evidence, and act quickly," Patel said in a statement. "This arrest demonstrates the strength and reach of our efforts to protect Americans from cybercrime."
The FBI did not provide any additional details on the individual's identity or the location of the arrest, but a U.S. official and another source briefed on the matter told CBS News the suspect was detained in Pennsylvania.
A law enforcement source said the suspect is a Canadian citizen and is believed to be directly involved in the hack of the FBI's website. That source said that other suspected co-conspirators remain at large.
The sources were granted anonymity to speak about law enforcement details that have not been made public.
The New York Times reported earlier Friday that the suspect was arrested in Pennsylvania on suspicion of being involved in the theft of FBI data.
An FBI spokesperson declined to comment on the details outlined in the New York Times report.
In a statement to CBS News, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police said it "is aware of the arrest of a Canadian in the US in connection with the ShinyHunters hack. The RCMP does not comment on investigations being conducted by other countries."
CBS News has reached out to other Canadian authorities for comment.
The FBI's jobs website was hacked in September, in what some veteran agents are saying may amount to the worst breach of a federal government system since the infamous hack of the Office of Personnel Management system in 2015, when more than 22 million government records were stolen.
ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for the FBI hack, the latest in a series of high-profile data breaches committed by the notorious group.
The hackers said they stole 2 to 3 terabytes of data related to FBI workers, a feat they accomplished thanks to a new vulnerability with Oracle PeopleSoft, a human resources management program.
Earlier this week, the FBI's Cyber Division's Assistant Director Brett Leatherman announced that following a review, the bureau determined that a contractor failed to implement a security patch to the system that was targeted.
"The FBI has removed the contractor and taken all necessary steps to both mitigate any further risk and protect our workforce," Leatherman said in a statement.
Reuters was the first to report on the contractor's removal, saying the individual worked at the company Accenture.
The arrest announced on Friday is the latest in a string of arrests of suspects who are believed to be tied to ShinyHunters.
On Sunday, that Jordanian authorities detained Saif al-Din Khader, who uses the online moniker "Rey" and is suspected to be involved in ShinyHunters.
A second suspected member of the group, identified as 24-year-old Pepijn van der Stap, was also arrested in Amsterdam, .
However, he was taken into custody on Sept. 15, meaning he was already in custody days before ShinyHunters announced it had hacked the FBI jobs website. The intrusion was first reported on Sept. 22 by 404 Media.
articles.summary:
The FBI has arrested a Canadian citizen in Pennsylvania suspected of involvement with the ShinyHunters cybercriminal group following a significant data breach of the bureau's jobs website.

### Key Points
- The suspect is accused of participating in the theft of 2 to 3 terabytes of FBI employee data via an Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability.
- FBI officials confirmed the breach occurred because a contractor failed to implement a necessary security patch on the targeted system.
- The bureau has terminated its relationship with the responsible contractor, identified in reports as an employee of Accenture.
- This arrest follows the recent detention of suspected ShinyHunters members Saif al-Din Khader in Jordan and Pepijn van der Stap in Amsterdam.
- The FBI continues to investigate the network, which is responsible for a series of high-profile data breaches targeting government and corporate systems.

### Why it Matters
This breach represents one of the most significant compromises of federal personnel data since the 2015 Office of Personnel Management hack. The incident highlights critical vulnerabilities in third-party contractor security protocols and underscores the ongoing challenges federal agencies face in protecting sensitive employee information from sophisticated cybercriminal syndicates.
